page: Amazon Web Services x2gd.16xlarge is a memory-optimized instance powered by 64-bit ARM architecture. The host utilizes AWS Graviton2 Neoverse-N1 processors running at 2.5 GHz across 64 dedicated physical cores without simultaneous multithreading. It provides an expansive 1024.0 GB of memory, equating to 16.0 GB per core, and includes 3800 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage alongside a 25 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. There are no discrete hardware GPUs attached.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong parallelized processing and cached throughput. In multi-core stress-ng testing, the instance registers in the top 25% with 97,052.9 points, paired with exceptional small-block cached read bandwidth of 3,783.24 GB/sec. Application testing shows top-tier throughput in Redis SET operations at 72.65 million operations per second and static web serving at 43.93 GB/sec, as well as high performance when compiling software via Clang. Conversely, single-threaded execution is relatively modest, as shown by lower Geekbench single-core scores (968.0), weak gzip compression (20.27 GB/sec), and reduced tokens-per-second rates during large language model inference.

From an infrastructure efficiency perspective, the dedicated 64-core Arm configuration maximizes memory density while eliminating hyperthreading resource contention. The bundled 3800 GB NVMe SSD storage reduces reliance on external network volumes for high-throughput scratchpads. Amazon Web Services x2gd.16xlarge is best suited for memory-intensive enterprise workloads, including large-scale in-memory databases like Redis or Memcached, big data caching layers, distributed ETL pipelines, and high-concurrency compilation services.
description: Amazon Web Services x2gd.16xlarge is an ARM-based, memory-optimized instance featuring 64 dedicated physical cores of AWS Graviton2 Neoverse-N1 processors clocked at 2.5 GHz. Configured with a massive 1024.0 GB of RAM—delivering 16.0 GB per vCPU—the system includes 3800 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage and 25 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, with zero GPUs. Benchmark profiles reveal exceptional multi-threaded scale and cached memory throughput, highlighted by top-quartile results in stress-ng multi-core testing, Clang compilation, and Redis SET benchmarks reaching 72.65 million operations per second. While single-thread instruction throughput and compression speeds are comparatively modest, the platform delivers high resource density and memory allocation per core without hyperthreading overhead. It is primarily fit for massive in-memory databases, distributed caching, real-time analytics, and heavy memory-bound data pipelines.
